description: Hope Canopus is an Iraqi youth science team registered with the Ministry of Youth & Sports, competing in NASA Space Apps Baghdad.
summary: FAST-ug is an 80-second, gravity-free neurological screening console designed to detect early stroke signs and acute neurological changes in astronauts during weightless spaceflight. On Earth, standard stroke assessments like the FAST protocol rely on gravity to reveal motor weakness—such as downward arm drift—and compare patients against terrestrial population averages. In microgravity, however, a weak limb can float level, cephalad fluid shifts alter baseline facial appearance, and transient neurological symptoms may vanish before ground specialists can evaluate the crew due to deep-space communication delays. FAST-ug solves this critical gap using a single standard webcam, zero wearables, and completely offline on-device computer vision. Through an interactive 80-second guided exam, the system tracks 478 facial, lip, hand, and ocular landmarks to measure side-to-side motor symmetry, rapid alternating movements (finger tapping and hand turning), speech articulation ("pa-ta-ka"), and gaze tracking. Crucially, rather than relying on Earth norms, FAST-ug compares each astronaut against their own rolling in-flight baseline built from two-minute daily alertness checks. When anomalies exceed statistical thresholds (z >= 2 for Watch; z >= 3 for Alert), it generates an immediate, side-specific clinical report and actionable guidance for the flight surgeon, capturing transient neurological evidence the moment it happens.

NOTE: HOW TO RUN THE PROJECT (WINDOWS)

No coding environment or IDE (such as VS Code) is required to run this application. To launch FAST-ug directly on your computer:

  1. Ensure Python 3.11 or 3.12 is installed on your Windows PC (make sure "Add python.exe to PATH" is checked during installation).
  2. Download the project files from our GitHub repository (https://github.com/khion213/FAST-ug) and extract the folder.
  3. Open the "fast_mug" folder and double-click the file named "run_windows.bat".
  4. The application will automatically set up its environment on the first launch and open the FAST-ug interface immediately. (If you want to test the system without a physical webcam, go to Settings inside the app and check "Use the simulated feed instead of a camera").

PROJECT OVERVIEW & CORE IDEA

Project Hope Canopus (FAST-ug), led by Khayoon Alaayedi and developed by the HOPE CANOPUS team (Zahraa Basheer, Rami Rashan, Falah Alaa, Imad Dheyab, and Jaafar Salim) in Baghdad, Iraq, is an 80-second, gravity-free neurological screening console designed to detect early stroke signs and acute neurological changes in astronauts during weightless spaceflight. On Earth, standard stroke checks depend on gravity (such as downward arm drift) and compare patients against terrestrial population averages. In microgravity, a weak limb can float level, fluid shifts alter baseline facial features, and transient symptoms can disappear before ground specialists can evaluate the crew due to deep-space communication delays. FAST-ug solves this problem using a single standard webcam, zero wearables, and 100% offline on-device computer vision. By tracking 478 facial, lip, hand, and eye landmarks and comparing each astronaut against their own rolling in-flight baseline, FAST-ug detects subtle lateralized neurological changes in 80 seconds and generates an immediate, actionable report for the flight surgeon.

WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

FAST-ug operates through two complementary, camera-only workflows designed for crew autonomy:

  1. Daily Alertness Check (2 Minutes): Routine checks measure blinking dynamics, PERCLOS (percentage of eyelid closure), and visual reaction time ("Look at the dot"). Each completed check refreshes the astronaut's personalized rolling baseline (median + Median Absolute Deviation across the last 10 checks) to separate genuine physiological drift from noisy measurements.
  2. Urgent 80-Second Guided Neuro Exam: Triggered immediately upon suspected symptoms, guiding the astronaut through four gravity-independent domains:
  • Face Symmetry: Evaluates resting mouth corner tilt, smile symmetry, eyebrow raise symmetry, and tight eye closure across 478 tracked facial points.
  • Speech & Articulation: Tracks lip motion symmetry, syllable pace ("pa-ta-ka"), and reading articulation during standardized phonetic prompts.
  • Gravity-Free Hand Motor Tasks: Replaces gravity-dependent arm-drift tests with rapid thumb-to-index finger tapping (measuring rate, amplitude, and tapping fatigue) and rapid alternating hand turning (pronation/supination symmetry).
  • Ocular & Gaze Tracking: Monitors horizontal smooth pursuit and saccadic accuracy as the crew member tracks a moving target ("Follow the dot") with a stationary head.
  1. Automated Triage & Flight Surgeon Briefing: Computes lateralized left-vs-right ratios and personal z-scores (z >= 2 Watch; z >= 3 Alert), outputting a clear status (Nominal, Watch, or Neurological Alert), timestamping symptom onset (critical for thrombolytic treatment windows), and exporting a structured Word report or encrypted SMTP ground-link brief.

KEY BENEFITS & IMPACT

  • 100% Gravity-Independent Assessment: Eliminates false negatives caused by limb buoyancy in microgravity by focusing on fine motor speed, amplitude decay, and bilateral symmetry.
  • Zero Additional Payload Mass: Uses existing spacecraft or laptop webcams, requiring no wearables, specialized sensors, or calibration hardware.
  • Deep-Space Autonomous Operation: Runs 100% offline on local hardware, overcoming Artemis, Lunar Gateway, and Mars communication latencies.
  • Preserves Transient Evidence: Captures objective quantitative metrics during brief episodes (such as Transient Ischemic Attacks) before symptoms resolve.
  • Personalized In-Flight Baselines: Adapts dynamically to each astronaut's fluid-shift and fatigue profile rather than relying on uncalibrated Earth norms.

TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION

  • Core Programming Language: Python 3.11 / 3.12
  • Computer Vision & Signal Processing: MediaPipe (478-point Face Mesh and Hand Landmarker models), OpenCV (opencv-python / opencv-contrib-python), NumPy, and SciPy for kinematic signal extraction, frequency/amplitude analysis, and MAD-based z-score statistics.
  • Desktop Interface & Data Visualization: PySide6 (Qt6) with High-DPI dark-mode console UI, Matplotlib for longitudinal trend charts, and python-docx for automated clinical report generation.
  • Communications & Storage: Local structured JSON/file storage (%APPDATA%\FAST-ug) with optional SMTP/SSL ground-link reporting and keyring credential protection.
  • Built-in Fault-Injection Simulator: Synthetic landmark engine capable of simulating Healthy, Left-sided weakness, and Fatigue scenarios for end-to-end validation.

CREATIVE INNOVATION

  • Physics-First Clinical Redesign: Instead of digitizing an Earth stroke checklist, we re-engineered neurological screening around orbital mechanics, substituting downward gravitational drift with bilateral kinematic symmetry and rapid alternating motor tasks.
  • Rolling Personal Digital Twin Baseline: By linking a 2-minute daily fatigue check to an emergency 80-second stroke exam, the software maintains a continuously updated neurological fingerprint for every crew member.
  • Actionable Clinical Decision Support: Goes beyond raw telemetry by recommending concrete next steps (recording exact symptom onset time, repeating the exam in 10 minutes to track progression, and guiding onboard ultrasound carotid/jugular assessment).

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS & RESPONSIBLE INNOVATION

  • Screening Aid, Not Autonomous Diagnosis: Clearly framed as a decision-support and evidence-capture tool to assist onboard crew medical officers and ground flight surgeons.
  • Acknowledged Scope Boundaries: Transparently documents that visual lip kinematics do not detect fluent aphasia without acoustic or semantic analysis, and that statistical baselines require at least three daily checks to stabilize.
  • Phased Validation Roadmap: Structured across four engineering stages: (1) Prototype and synthetic landmark simulator, (2) Controlled ground clinical studies, (3) Head-down tilt bed-rest analogues simulating cephalad fluid shifts, and (4) Parabolic-flight microgravity evaluation.

INTENDED GLOBAL IMPACT

  • Space Exploration (Artemis & Deep Space): Protects crew neuro-health on long-duration missions to the Moon, Lunar Gateway, and Mars where real-time telemedicine is impossible.
  • Terrestrial Telemedicine & Rural Healthcare: Because FAST-ug runs offline on a basic webcam in 80 seconds, it can be deployed in remote clinics, ambulances, rural communities, and elder-care facilities lacking immediate access to neurologists.
